dedupe_keys.name: stips serbia agricultural market information system weekly bulletins of fruit and vegetable livestock grain and feed prices 2004 to 2026 and monthly input prices

description: STIPS is Serbia's agricultural market information system, run by the Ministry of Agriculture since 2004. The system publishes two weekly bulletins: one for fruit and vegetables and one for live animals, cereals and animal feed. The bulletin archive runs from 2004 to week 38 of 2026, and the site also posts monthly prices of farm inputs such as pesticides and fertilisers and weekly summaries of trade on the Novi Sad commodity exchange. Coverage is national. The bulletins are free and available to download as PDF; no licence terms are stated. Caveats: prices are in PDF bulletins, not a database, markets and products covered have changed over two decades, and methods are not documented on the pages read. Simulation uses: building long weekly food price series to study shocks such as droughts, floods and the 2022 grain price spike, and calibrating food system resilience models for Serbia and the western Balkans. Related records: the WFP global food prices (data-wfp-global-food-prices) cover Serbian markets less densely, and Hungary's AKI price system (data-aki-hungary-market-price-information-system) is the neighbouring national source.
